faqs.q: How long does an EPDM rubber roof last on a Nutley building?

runs.v: An EPDM rubber roof lasts 15 to 25 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, and other sources say EPDM systems can last 20 to 30 years with maintenance. On Nutley's porch, dormer, and addition flats, the first failures show up as seam separation and flashing wear at the wall transition, not in the rubber field.

faqs.q: Does an EPDM roof on my Nutley home or commercial building need a permit?

runs.v: Replacing the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit, so confirm the scope with the Township of Nutley construction office before work.

faqs.q: Does a historic district restrict EPDM roofing work in Nutley?

runs.v: It can. Exterior roofing on a property in a locally designated historic district can need a separate historic-preservation review in addition to the construction permit, so confirm the parcel with the Township of Nutley before work. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no restriction on a private property owner.

faqs.q: Can you patch the EPDM on my Nutley porch or rear addition instead of replacing it?

runs.v: Yes, when the damage stays localized on a porch, dormer, or rear-addition flat. A Newark Quality Roofing service cleans the area, applies EPDM primer, and adheres a rubber patch or reseams the lap, per HomeGuide membrane-repair guidance; replacement follows when the membrane reaches the end of its service life or failures spread across the deck.

faqs.q: Why does my Nutley EPDM roof keep leaking at the same seam?

runs.v: Seam separation is the most common EPDM failure mode, because the adhesive joining two sheets breaks down before the rubber field does, per HomeGuide membrane-repair guidance. Shrinkage at porch, dormer, and addition wall transitions comes second, so Newark Quality Roofing checks the seams first, then the flashing, and reseals the failed lap.
